416	    def diff_at(self, name_a: str, name_b: str, at: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
417	        """Diff two branches' current heads as of ``at``.
418	
419	        Both names and ``at`` are validated (in signature order) before
420	        either branch is looked up; the diff itself is delegated to
421	        :meth:`EventGraph.diff_at` on the branches' current heads. The
422	        query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
423	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
424	        from internal state.
425	        """
426	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
427	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
428	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
429	        if at_value < 0:
430	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
431	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
432	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)

437	    def compare(self, name_a: str, name_b: str) -> dict[str, object]:
438	        """Compare the ancestor closures of two branches' current heads.
439	
440	        Both names are validated (in signature order) before either
441	        branch is looked up: non-``str`` names raise :class:`TypeError`,
442	        empty names raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
443	        :class:`KeyError`, and comparing a branch with itself raises
444	        :class:`ValueError`. Each head's ancestor closure is taken once,
445	        in the graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` replay
446	        order. The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
447	        ``common, left_only, right_only, fork``: tuples of event ids for
448	        the intersection, the left-only and the right-only events
449	        (common and left-only in left replay order, right-only in right
450	        replay order), plus ``fork`` -- the last common id in left replay
451	        order, or ``None`` when the closures share no event. The query
452	        is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are never
453	        modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached from
454	        internal state.
455	        """
456	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
457	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
458	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
459	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
460	        if name_a == name_b:
461	            raise ValueError(f"cannot compare branch {name_a!r} with itself")
462	
463	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
464	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
465	        left_ids = set(left_order)
466	        right_ids = set(right_order)
467	
468	        common = tuple(
469	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id in right_ids
470	        )
471	        left_only = tuple(
472	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id not in right_ids
473	        )
474	        right_only = tuple(
475	            event_id for event_id in right_order if event_id not in left_ids
476	        )
477	        return {
478	            "common": common,
479	            "left_only": left_only,
480	            "right_only": right_only,
481	            "fork": common[-1] if common else None,
482	        }

484	    def attribute_divergence(
485	        self, name_a: str, name_b: str, key: str
486	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
487	        """Attribute the cross-branch divergence of ``key`` to its causes.
488	
489	        Both names and ``key`` are validated (in signature order) before
490	        either branch is looked up: non-``str`` values raise
491	        :class:`TypeError`, empty strings raise :class:`ValueError`,
492	        unknown branches raise :class:`KeyError` (``name_a`` first), and
493	        naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`. Each
494	        branch's current head ancestor closure is replayed in the graph's
495	        parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order; a side on which
496	        ``key`` never appears contributes the value ``0``.
497	
498	        The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
499	        ``key, fork, left, right``: ``key`` is the queried key as given
500	        and ``fork`` is the last common event id in left replay order (or
501	        ``None`` when the closures share no event). ``left`` and ``right``
502	        are fresh dicts whose keys are ordered ``value, cause, path,
503	        affected``: the replayed integer value, the cause event id, and
504	        data derived from it. When the two values differ, a side's cause
505	        is the first event exclusive to that side whose changes contain
506	        ``key`` (zero deltas included) in that side's replay order, or
507	        ``None`` when no such event exists; when the values are equal,
508	        both causes are ``None``. ``path`` is the tuple of ids on the
509	        shortest parent-to-child path from the cause to that side's
510	        current head (both ends included), ties broken by the Unicode
511	        code point order of the complete id tuples, and ``affected`` is
512	        the tuple of the cause's strict descendant ids in that side's
513	        replay order; both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``.
514	        The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
515	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
516	        from internal state.
517	        """
518	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
519	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
520	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
521	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
522	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
523	        if name_a == name_b:
524	            raise ValueError(
525	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
526	                "against itself"
527	            )
528	
529	        return self._attribute_divergence_for(
530	            self._heads[name_a], self._heads[name_b], key
531	        )

533	    def attribute_divergence_at(
534	        self,
535	        name_a: str,
536	        node_a: str,
537	        name_b: str,
538	        node_b: str,
539	        key: str,
540	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
541	        """Attribute the divergence of ``key`` at two historical nodes.
542	
543	        This is the historical-node form of :meth:`attribute_divergence`:
544	        instead of each branch's current head, the left side replays the
545	        ancestor closure of ``node_a`` on branch ``name_a`` and the right
546	        side that of ``node_b`` on branch ``name_b``. All five parameters
547	        are validated in signature order (``name_a``, ``node_a``,
548	        ``name_b``, ``node_b``, ``key``) before either node is replayed:
549	        non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty strings raise
550	        :class:`ValueError`; the branches are then looked up in order
551	        (``name_a`` first), an unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError`,
552	        and naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`; a
553	        node absent from the graph, or outside its named branch's current
554	        head ancestor closure (``node_a`` checked before ``node_b``),
555	        raises :class:`KeyError`.
556	
557	        Each node's ancestor closure is replayed in the graph's
558	        parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order; a side on which
559	        ``key`` never appears contributes the value ``0``. The result is
560	        a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``key, fork, left, right``:
561	        ``key`` is the queried key as given, ``fork`` is the last common
562	        event id in left replay order (or ``None`` when the closures
563	        share no event), and ``left``/``right`` are fresh dicts whose
564	        keys are ordered ``value, cause, path, affected``. When the two
565	        values differ, a side's cause is the first event exclusive to
566	        that side whose changes contain ``key`` (zero deltas included)
567	        in that side's replay order, or ``None`` when no such event
568	        exists; when the values are equal, both causes are ``None``.
569	        ``path`` is the tuple of ids on the shortest parent-to-child
570	        path from the cause to that side's node (both ends included),
571	        ties broken by the Unicode code point order of the complete id
572	        tuples, and ``affected`` is the tuple of the cause's strict
573	        descendant ids within that side's closure in its replay order;
574	        both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``. The query is
575	        read-only: success or failure never modifies the graph, branch
576	        heads, audit or idempotency records, and the returned dict and
577	        tuples are detached from internal state.
578	        """
579	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
580	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
581	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
582	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
583	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
584	
585	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
586	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
587	        if name_a == name_b:
588	            raise ValueError(
589	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
590	                "against itself"
591	            )
592	
593	        if node_a not in self._graph._at:
594	            raise KeyError(node_a)
595	        if node_a not in set(
596	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
597	        ):
598	            raise KeyError(node_a)
599	        if node_b not in self._graph._at:
600	            raise KeyError(node_b)
601	        if node_b not in set(
602	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
603	        ):
604	            raise KeyError(node_b)
605	
606	        return self._attribute_divergence_for(node_a, node_b, key)

608	    def attribute_divergences_at(
609	        self,
610	        name_a: str,
611	        node_a: str,
612	        name_b: str,
613	        node_b: str,
614	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
615	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
616	        """Attribute divergences for several keys at two historical nodes.
617	
618	        The multi-key form of :meth:`attribute_divergence_at`: all five
619	        parameters are validated before either node is replayed. The four
620	        string parameters are checked in signature order (``name_a``,
621	        ``node_a``, ``name_b``, ``node_b``): non-``str`` values raise
622	        :class:`TypeError` and empty strings raise :class:`ValueError`.
623	        ``keys`` must be a tuple (else :class:`TypeError`); its elements
624	        are checked in input order, and a non-``str`` element raises
625	        :class:`TypeError`, while an empty or duplicated key raises
626	        :class:`ValueError`. The branches are then looked up in order
627	        (``name_a`` first): an unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError` and
628	        naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`; a node
629	        absent from the graph, or outside its named branch's current head
630	        ancestor closure (``node_a`` checked before ``node_b``), raises
631	        :class:`KeyError`. Branch and node checks run even when ``keys``
632	        is empty, in which case an empty tuple is returned.
633	
634	        Every key is answered from one read-only historical view: both
635	        nodes' ancestor closures are taken once before results are built.
636	        The returned tuple has one fresh dict per key, ordered by the
637	        Unicode code point of the keys (independent of their input
638	        order); item-wise, each dict equals the result of
639	        :meth:`attribute_divergence_at` with the same first four
640	        arguments and that key, preserving its key order, types and full
641	        semantics. The dicts and tuples neither share objects with each
642	        other nor alias internal state. Success or failure never modifies
643	        the graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
644	        """
645	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
646	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
647	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
648	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
649	        if not isinstance(keys, tuple):
650	            raise TypeError(
651	                f"keys must be a tuple, got {type(keys).__name__}"
652	            )
653	        seen_keys: set[str] = set()
654	        for key in keys:
655	            self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
656	            if key in seen_keys:
657	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate key {key!r}")
658	            seen_keys.add(key)
659	
660	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
661	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
662	        if name_a == name_b:
663	            raise ValueError(
664	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
665	                "against itself"
666	            )
667	
668	        # Capture the read-only historical view before any node is
669	        # replayed: the branches' current head closures decide node
670	        # membership, and the nodes' own closures answer every key.
671	        head_closure_a = set(
672	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
673	        )
674	        head_closure_b = set(
675	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
676	        )
677	        if node_a not in self._graph._at or node_a not in head_closure_a:
678	            raise KeyError(node_a)
679	        if node_b not in self._graph._at or node_b not in head_closure_b:
680	            raise KeyError(node_b)
681	
682	        if not keys:
683	            return ()
684	
685	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_a)
686	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_b)
687	        return tuple(
688	            self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(
689	                left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b, key
690	            )
691	            for key in sorted(keys)
692	        )

694	    def divergence_timeline(
695	        self,
696	        name_a: str,
697	        name_b: str,
698	        points: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...],
699	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
700	    ) -> tuple[tuple[dict[str, object], ...], ...]:
701	        """Attribute divergences for several node pairs and keys at once.
702	
703	        The multi-point form of :meth:`attribute_divergences_at`:
704	        ``points`` is a tuple of ``(node_a, node_b)`` pairs, each played
705	        against the same two branches -- the left nodes live on
706	        ``name_a``'s current head ancestor closure and the right nodes on
707	        ``name_b``'s.
708	
709	        All four parameters are validated in signature order
710	        (``name_a``, ``name_b``, ``points``, ``keys``); containers are
711	        walked in input order, and all of this finishes before any state
712	        is consulted. The names raise :class:`TypeError` when not
713	        ``str`` and :class:`ValueError` when empty. ``points`` and
714	        ``keys`` must be tuples (else :class:`TypeError`); a point that

717	        non-``str`` nodes and keys raise :class:`TypeError`, empty
718	        strings raise :class:`ValueError`, and a repeated node pair or
719	        key (in input order) raises :class:`ValueError`.
720	
721	        The branches are then looked up in order (``name_a`` first): an
722	        unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError` and naming the same
723	        branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`. Nodes are checked per
724	        pair, left before right, pairs in ``points`` order: a node
725	        absent from the graph or outside its named branch's current
726	        head ancestor closure raises :class:`KeyError`. With empty
727	        ``points`` the names, keys and branches are still validated and
728	        an empty tuple is returned; with empty ``keys`` every node is
729	        still validated and each point contributes an empty tuple.
730	
731	        Every point and key is answered from one read-only historical
732	        view: both branches' current head closures and every node's own
733	        closure are taken once before results are built. The outer
734	        tuple follows ``points`` in its original order; each point
735	        contributes a tuple of one fresh dict per key, ordered by the
736	        Unicode code point of the keys (independent of their input
737	        order), item-wise equal to calling
738	        :meth:`attribute_divergences_at` with that node pair and
739	        ``keys`` -- preserving its dict key order, types and full
740	        attribution semantics. The tuples and dicts at every level are
741	        freshly built, neither sharing objects with each other nor
742	        aliasing internal state. Success or failure never modifies the
743	        graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
744	        """
745	        # --- Parameters validated in signature order, containers in
746	        # input order, before any state is consulted. ---
747	        ordered_points, keys = self._divergence_inputs(
748	            name_a, name_b, points, keys
749	        )
750	        if ordered_points is None:
751	            return ()
752	
753	        return tuple(
754	            tuple(
755	                self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(
756	                    left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b, key
757	                )
758	                for key in sorted(keys)
759	            )
760	            for left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b in ordered_points
761	        )

763	    def divergence_summary(
764	        self,
765	        name_a: str,
766	        name_b: str,
767	        points: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...],
768	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
769	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
770	        """Summarize how each key diverges and converges across node pairs.
771	
772	        Shares :meth:`divergence_timeline`'s parameters, validation order
773	        and errors, empty-container handling and branch/node closure rules
774	        exactly: the four parameters are validated in signature order
775	        (``name_a``, ``name_b``, ``points``, ``keys``), containers walked
776	        in input order, before any state is consulted; non-``str`` values
777	        raise :class:`TypeError`, empty strings :class:`ValueError`,
778	        ``points``/``keys`` that are not tuples or points that are not
779	        length-2 tuples raise :class:`TypeError`, and a repeated node pair
780	        or key raises :class:`ValueError`. Branches are then looked up in
781	        order (unknown branch :class:`KeyError`, same branch twice
782	        :class:`ValueError`), and nodes are checked per pair, left before
783	        right, pairs in ``points`` order (:class:`KeyError` when absent

787	        historical view as :meth:`divergence_timeline`: both branches'
788	        current head closures and every node's own closure are taken once
789	        before results are built. Points are indexed from ``0`` in their
790	        given order. For each key (ordered by Unicode code point,
791	        independent of input order) the result is a fresh dict whose keys
792	        are ordered ``key, first_diverged, transitions, last``:
793	
794	        ``first_diverged`` is the index of the first point whose left and
795	        right replayed values for the key differ, or ``None`` when they are
796	        equal at every point. ``transitions`` lists, in point-index order,
797	        every state change between adjacent points (plus divergence at the
798	        first point): each item is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
799	        ``index, kind, left_value, right_value, left_cause, right_cause``.
800	        ``kind`` is ``diverged`` when the first point already diverges or
801	        equality becomes divergence, ``converged`` when divergence becomes
802	        equality, and ``reattributed`` when adjacent points both diverge
803	        but either attributed cause changes; adjacent points with no such
804	        change record nothing. The values and causes are those of the
805	        attribution at ``index``. ``last`` is a detached deep copy of the
806	        complete attribution dict for the key at the final point (the
807	        ``key, fork, left, right`` structure of

812	        yields an empty tuple; empty ``keys`` still validates every node
813	        and yields an empty tuple. The tuples and dicts at every level are
814	        freshly built, neither sharing objects with each other nor aliasing
815	        internal state. Success or failure never modifies the graph,
816	        branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
817	        """

819	            name_a, name_b, points, keys
820	        )

822	            return ()
823	        return self._divergence_summaries(ordered_points, keys)

825	    def divergence_matrix(
826	        self,
827	        reference: str,
828	        series: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]],
829	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
830	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
831	        """Run :meth:`divergence_summary` for several branches at once.
832	
833	        Each entry of ``series`` pairs a branch name with its own tuple of
834	        ``(reference node, series node)`` points, every point replayed
835	        against the same ``reference`` branch -- the left node must live on
836	        the reference branch's current head ancestor closure and the right
837	        node on the named series branch's.
838	
839	        ``reference`` is validated first: a non-``str`` value raises
840	        :class:`TypeError` and an empty string :class:`ValueError`.
841	        ``series`` must be a dict (else :class:`TypeError`); its keys are
842	        checked in insertion order, a non-``str`` series name raising
843	        :class:`TypeError` and an empty or ``reference``-equal name
844	        raising :class:`ValueError`, and each series' points are walked in
845	        input order. ``keys`` is checked last, exactly as in
846	        :meth:`divergence_summary`: it must be a tuple (else
847	        :class:`TypeError`), a non-``str`` element raises :class:`TypeError`,
848	        and an empty or duplicated key raises :class:`ValueError`. The rest
849	        of the validation, errors, empty-container handling and
850	        branch/node closure rules are exactly
851	        :meth:`divergence_summary`'s for the corresponding
852	        ``(reference, series_name, points, keys)`` call: points must be a
853	        tuple of length-2 node-id tuples with no repeated pair, and all
854	        inputs finish validating before the branches are looked up,
855	        reference first and then the series in ``series`` insertion order
856	        (unknown branch :class:`KeyError`, a node absent from the graph or
857	        the named branch's current head closure :class:`KeyError`, left
858	        before right, pairs in points order).
859	
860	        Every series, point and key is answered from one shared read-only
861	        historical view: the reference branch's and every series branch's
862	        current head closures and every node's own closure are taken once
863	        before results are built. The returned tuple follows ``series`` in
864	        its insertion order; each entry is a fresh dict whose keys are
865	        ordered ``branch, summaries, reconverged``: ``branch`` is the
866	        series branch name, ``summaries`` is the tuple of fresh summary
867	        dicts item-wise equal to :meth:`divergence_summary` for that series
868	        (keyed and ordered as there), and ``reconverged`` is a tuple of
869	        booleans aligned with ``summaries`` (keys in Unicode code point
870	        order) -- each is ``True`` exactly when the summary's
871	        ``first_diverged`` is not ``None`` and the two sides' values in its
872	        ``last`` attribution are equal. An empty ``series`` still
873	        validates ``reference`` and ``keys`` and looks the reference branch
874	        up, yielding an empty tuple; empty ``keys`` still validates every
875	        node, and each series then contributes empty
876	        ``summaries``/``reconverged`` tuples. The tuples and dicts at every
877	        level are freshly built, neither sharing objects with each other
878	        nor aliasing internal state. Success or failure never modifies the
879	        graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
880	        """
881	        # --- All inputs finish validating before any branch is looked up,
882	        # mirroring divergence_summary's reference, branch, points, keys
883	        # order with series walked in insertion order. ---
884	        self._require_nonempty_str(reference, "reference")
885	        if not isinstance(series, dict):
886	            raise TypeError(
887	                f"series must be a dict, got {type(series).__name__}"
888	            )
889	        per_series: list[tuple[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]]] = []
890	        for series_name, series_points in series.items():
891	            self._require_nonempty_str(series_name, "series branch")
892	            if series_name == reference:
893	                raise ValueError(
894	                    f"series branch {series_name!r} cannot equal reference "
895	                    f"branch {reference!r}"
896	                )
897	            self._validate_points(series_points)
898	            per_series.append((series_name, series_points))
